## How they got there
Inter secured their place as the 2022-23 runner-up by navigating a knockout phase containing 16 teams before ultimately losing the final to Manchester City 0-1. Their path was defined by exceptional efficiency in front of goal rather than dominance in possession or volume of play. They recorded a shot accuracy of 59.3%, placing them at the 97th percentile against that season's teams and the 90th percentile across all Champions League history since 2011-12. This precision was complemented by a shot conversion rate of 18.5%, which ranked in the 62nd percentile for their peers and the 74th percentile historically. Despite these offensive sharpness metrics, they operated with only 40.8 attacks per game and 470 passes per game, figures that sit at the 41st and 42nd percentiles respectively against that season's competition.

## Would the model have picked them?
The predictive model would almost certainly not have selected Inter as a finalist contender. With a calculated probability of just 2.9% to reach the final, they ranked only 14th out of the 16 knockout teams in that specific season. This stands in stark contrast to the base rate, which indicates a random knockout team has a 12.5% chance of reaching the summit. The model's expectation for their performance was equally low, projecting an expected stage value of only 0.09, effectively predicting they would exit before the quarter-finals. While their shot accuracy and conversion were elite, these strengths were insufficient to overcome significant negative signals in other areas, resulting in a prediction that fell far short of their actual achievement.

## Weak spots
The primary factors dragging down Inter's predicted performance were their low volume of offensive output and limited ball circulation. The model heavily penalized them for generating only 40.8 attacks per game, which contributed -0.22 to their expected knockout stage score. This lack of sustained pressure was mirrored by a pass volume of just 470 per game, contributing another -0.12 to the negative projection. Additionally, their goal difference per game stood at only 0.5, a figure that resulted in a -0.15 SHAP contribution. These statistical deficiencies suggest the model viewed them as a team lacking the consistent dominance required for deep tournament runs, despite their ability to convert chances when they did occur.

Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events or numbers that are not in the facts. Percentiles compare a team with other Champions League teams: 90 means higher than 90% of them. For stats marked '(lower is better)', a LOW percentile is good. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: +0.30 means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by 0.30 of a round. Write plain markdown without tables.
